newsitem.title: UK: PET threat to aluminium greater in mature markets.
newsitem.headline: PET threat to aluminium greater in mature markets.

text.p: The threat to aluminium in packaging comes more from mature areas, rather than emerging markets, Nick Mason, research manager aluminium at industry analysts CRU International said.
PET beverage packaging has taken a significant lead in innovation over the can, which has been re-inforced by costs advantages.

"Most importantly for the can and can stock community the innovations in PET packaging which were largely pioneered in the U.S. have been disseminated very rapidly indeed to the other developed markets and look likely to spread worldwide as fast," Mason said in a speech prepared for delivery to the Financial Times World Aluminium Conference.
The threat to the aluminium can in certain emerging markets is less acute, as many are developing along different lines to the U.S.

In markets where still soft drinks, teas and coffees are preferred to carbonated soft drinks, and beer consumption is rising strongly as well, PET packaging will be less of a threat to the aluminium can, he added.
